brief.headline: Lead with supply security and a second source — they're in the distress zone (health D 0/100, lost ₹-22.50 Cr in FY2023-24) — then ask for the ₹1.62/NOS price we already pay elsewhere.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹1.62/NOS on the LDPE bottle, the price we already pay Bprex.
priceAsk.basis: We pay Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited ₹1.62/NOS for the same LDPE BOTTLE 5ML WHITE OPAQUE; Berry charges ₹1.69/NOS — a 4.3% markup we shouldn't carry. They're 100% a trader (not the maker), so their price has a reseller margin built in — push them to the manufacturer's level.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 Days After Receipt — don't offer faster payment to a supplier this fragile.

brief.financialLeverage: Berry is very weak: they lost ₹-22.50 Cr in FY2023-24, score D (0/100) for money health, owe 220.44 times their own cash, and sit in the distress zone (Altman Z -0.18). Their cash is stuck for 335 days, far longer than similar firms (70 days), so cash is extremely tight. We're a big customer — our ₹81.39 L is 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr revenue — but that size cuts both ways: a hard squeeze could tip them over and kill our supply. Lead with supply security (audit, qualify a backup) and frame the price ask as fair benchmarking, not a test of strength.

evidence.point: We're a big slice of their business
Their cash is stuck far longer than rivals
We're paying more than our best price

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate and financially robust.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) making pails, containers, pharma packaging — a strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited
alternates.why: Already our supplier for the same LDPE bottle at ₹1.62/NOS — proven, cheaper, and a live backup if Berry can't match the price.

risks: They're in the distress zone (Altman Z -0.18) and lost ₹-22.50 Cr last year — pushing too hard on price could break them and leave us scrambling for supply mid-quarter.
They're 100% a trader, not the maker — if they fold or lose their own supplier, we have no direct line to the factory; line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek now.
We're 7.21% of their revenue — big enough that losing us hurts them, but also big enough that if they go under we lose ₹81.39 L of committed supply overnight.
Their cash is stuck for 335 days vs 70 days for peers — they're chronically short of cash, so any payment hiccup on our side (late PO, disputed invoice) will escalate fast.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but we need to talk about two things: getting you audited so we can confidently grow the business together, and closing the ₹0.07/piece gap to the ₹1.62 price we already pay Bprex for the same bottle.
